name: Flecainide
summary: A potent sodium channel blocker highly effective for atrial fibrillation and supraventricular tachycardias — strictly limited to patients without structural heart disease.
mechanism: Use-dependent blockade of cardiac sodium channels, slowing atrial and ventricular conduction (QRS widening) with little effect on refractoriness; mild potassium channel block.
pharmacodynamics: Slows conduction velocity; prolongs PR and QRS intervals; mild negative inotropic effect.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic (CYP2D6) plus renal excretion of unchanged drug (~30%)

dosing.adult: 100 mg every 12 h (range 50–150 mg every 12 h); IV 1–2 mg/kg over 10 min for conversion of atrial fibrillation
dosing.renalAdjustment: Start at 50 mg every 12 h if CrCl <35 mL/min

safety.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed (no adequate data)
contraindications: Structural heart disease or coronary artery disease (CAST trial — increased mortality post-MI)
Second- or third-degree AV block or bifascicular block without pacemaker
warnings: Proarrhythmia — never use in structural/ischemic heart disease (CAST)
Negative inotrope — may worsen heart failure
QRS widening >25% from baseline — reduce dose
monitoring: Flecainide trough levels (0.2–1.0 µg/mL) in renal/hepatic disease
Echocardiogram if structural disease is suspected
safety.overdose: Supportive care; sodium bicarbonate for widened QRS

indications: Sustained ventricular tachycardia only in patients without structural heart disease
clinicalPearls: The CAST trial showed increased mortality in post-MI patients — verify no structural/ischemic heart disease before use.
CYP2D6 poor metabolizers and drugs like amiodarone raise flecainide levels.
good: Younger patients with structurally normal hearts and paroxysmal AF/SVT.
bad: Any patient with coronary disease, prior MI, or impaired ventricular function.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
